safety_nets.verdict: 2026-11-20: on the nuclear basket's worst 10% of days (avg -4.7%), only VIX futures (+5.1%, but -46%/yr when held), inverse Nasdaq (+1.7%, -14.6%/yr) and inverse S&P (+1.3%, -11.8%/yr) rose; dollar/Treasuries ~0; gold, utilities, energy, defense, gas, coal, bitcoin all FELL. Basket-level switches (cash or 50% inverse when sector falling) did not reduce the worst drop (-50% to -55%) and cut returns. Trade-level stops + no buys in a falling sector remain the working safety net (-46% -> -14% in the trade backtest).

reactor_outages.verdict: 2026-11-20: 174 reactor outages at CEG/VST/TLN units since listing (NRC daily power 2019-2026; outage = >=80% to <=30%). Stock vs peers on report day, +1, +5, +10 days: CEG (25 units, n=116) ~0 everywhere (p>0.19). VST n=49 / TLN n=9 show +0.5 to +4.9% but driven by VST's 2024 run vs peers and tiny TLN sample; 32 tests, nothing survives. Verdict: a single outage is not a tradable signal. Keep as context (fleet % running, open outages) and re-test when a big multi-unit or long unplanned outage happens.

big_move_followthrough.verdict: 2026-11-20: 1,094 big days (|move|>=2.5 sd or 8%) in the 10 stocks since 2019 (research/big_moves.csv), split market / sector / company-only. Company-only UP spikes fade: -0.7% next day, -1.5% over 5 days, -2.0% over 20 vs the basket (n=370, p<0.02, both halves; 7 of 10 stocks, strongest DNN/NXE/UEC/UUUU/CCJ). Use: don't buy right after a lone spike, let it come back to support. Other buckets: nothing that holds in both halves.

panic_day_rebound.verdict: 2026-11-20 PROMISING (not proven): buy at the close when the market (SPY) falls 2%+, the stock falls 3%+ and is 15%+ below its 20-day high (CCJ Nov 5 2026 type). 61 distinct days since 2019: hold 4 days +3.6% avg / +3.3% median, up 62%; hold 6 days +5.3% / +6.2%, up 70% (p=0.001 by day), positive every year. Risk: when the panic is the start of a crash (Feb-Mar 2020, May 2022) it loses 15-21% and stops don't help (gaps). Buying next morning instead of the close keeps much less (+0.9% over 2 days). ~23 variants tried, so treat as a candidate for paper testing. | 2026-11-20 filters tried (first vs repeat panic, market vs 200-day avg, market drawdown, size of market/stock drop; 10 more trials): none removes the crash days cleanly, splits are 4-15 days and flip between halves. Kept the simple rule; protection = size (15% each, 45% total, 3 names). Now trading on paper as strategy #2. | 2026-11-20 round 3 (25 more trials): which 3 to pick barely matters (deepest-under-high +6.0% vs biggest-drop +5.3%, noise); VIX 40+ days best (+9.3%, 85% up, n=13); SECTOR-only panics have no edge (+0.6%), it needs the whole market; fixed 6-day hold best avg, but sell at +10% close or day 6 = +5.0% avg, 72% up, worst -17.5% (vs -21.4%) and frees cash sooner -> adopted. Non-panic swings: best is -10% in 3 days in a calm market, +2.1% over 6d vs +1.0% for any day, steady in both halves (practice candidate only). | 2026-11-23 exits (3 trials, 153 trades on 61 days): sell at +10% on a CLOSE or day 6 = +5.8% avg (71% up) beats a resting +10% limit (+4.4%, 75% up), a +8% limit (+3.7%) and a give-back guard (+5.5%); both halves agree. Winners often run past +10%, so selling intraday cuts them. No change: keep the close rule, no stop (crash-day gaps go straight through stops). | 2026-11-23 sizing (5 trials, $1,000 compounded 2019-2026 incl. 2020 crash): 15%/45% -> $2,248 (10.8%/yr, worst drop -16.5%); 25%/75% -> $3,666 (17.9%, -26.8%); 33%/100% -> $5,023 (22.7%, -34.5%); 50%/100% -> $5,832 (25.0%, -45.2%); 100% one name -> $10,767 (35.1%, -45.5%, only 44 trades: rides on single picks). Every year positive at every size. Owner chose to compound harder: ADOPTED 33% each / 100% total on paper. Panic days are rare (75 of 1,985 sessions), so cash sits idle most days; 3-down-days as an idle-cash setup: +1.66% over 5d vs +0.84% any day, 55% up, too weak alone.

ccj_daily_reversal.verdict: 2026-11-20: CCJ day-to-day moves are close to random (autocorrelation -0.02). After up/down days of 3-5%, 5-8%, 8%+ and gap-and-reverse days, the next 1-3 days show no reliable bounce-back (p 0.19-0.95). The 'jumps up then back down' pattern is visible but not predictable from the day's move alone; across all 10 stocks, company-only up spikes do fade (see big_move_followthrough).

panic_rebound_calls_estimate.verdict: 2026-11-20 ESTIMATE (Black-Scholes, implied vol = 1.3x recent vol on entry, 1.05x on exit, ~5% spread each way; no real historical option prices): 2-week calls on the panic-day picks turn the stock's +5.2% into about +5% (at the money) or 0% (5% out of the money) on average, median -9% to -16%, winning on <50% of days, losing 80%+ on 11-15%. Fear makes options expensive exactly on panic days. Shares beat calls for this setup. Re-test with the options recorder's real chains once enough panic days are recorded. Today's real CCJ chain: IV ~60%, $65 Dec-4 call 0.65/0.97 (40% spread).

volume_profile_levels.verdict: 2026-11-22 ADOPTED as a filter. From an order-flow video (value area / point of control). 9,877 Patient Levels practice trades 2024-2026, 52 stocks, profile = last 140 hourly bars before the decision, exact limit price. Levels BELOW the value area: -0.055R, 29% wins (n=2,177); in a THIN volume zone: 0.000R, 31% (n=2,627); inside value +0.382R; at the heaviest price +0.284R (44% wins); thick zone +0.330R. Skipping below-value or thin: kept +0.331R / 41% wins vs skipped +0.007R / 31%, both halves (old +0.43/+0.03, new +0.23/-0.01), 85% of tickers agree; nuclear 10 kept +0.279R vs skipped -0.019R. The video's specific claim (reversals at the value-area LOW) did NOT hold: +0.107R, below average. First attempt used the fill bar's low (look-ahead) and overstated it; corrected.

macro_drivers.verdict: 2026-11-23: big daily moves in natural gas (+/-5%), oil (+/-4%), the dollar (+/-0.8%), the 10-year yield (+/-10bp) and the VIX (+20%/-15%) since 2019, tested on every stock vs the basket over 5 and 20 days, same-week moves counted once. None passes the correction yet. Closest: gas jumps -> miners trail the basket by about 0.9% over 20 days (780 weeks, both halves); rate jumps help power names in the newer half only (+5.8% vs -0.9%) = not stable. News split by the first day's reaction (cheered / punished): nothing holds yet. Tested nightly as data grows.
